title: MongoDB: collections, documents and the schema that exists anyway

videos.script: MongoDB is the first of the three servers you get to know properly. It stores documents, and a document looks like JSON. {{document}} It is not JSON. It is BSON, with types JSON never had: a date, a 64-bit integer, an exact decimal for money. {{types}} Multiply 349.90 by three in a JavaScript shell and you get a price that ends in nines. The decimal type gives you 1049.70. {{money}} Then you write. Products, orders, and the operators that change one field without rewriting the rest. {{crud}} And you meet the claim people make about MongoDB, that it has no schema. {{schemaless}} Insert a price as a string and the server says yes. Misspell a field and it says yes. Misspell the collection, and it makes you a new one. {{typos}} The schema did not go away. It moved into every program that reads the data, and it fails there, much later. {{later}} So the lesson ends with the server refusing on your behalf: a JSON Schema validator, the error it gives, and a way to switch it on without breaking a collection you already have. {{validator}}
